quest.title: Dual Evidence
quest.description: While in Aaru Village, you meet another Vahumana researcher named Kalantari. He has been fretting over his paper lately and is seeking help...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x500, Primogem x60, Mora x40000, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're back at Aaru Village again. Whoa! This place is still burning hot, just like how it was on our first visit.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon wonders how Jeht and Tirzad are doing... Paimon's kinda concerned.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yes, that's what Paimon thinks too, even if we're just speculating here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The last expedition should have helped with their composure, or... should we say that they're growing up?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm not sure if we can call what Tirzad did "growing up"...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But Jeht said that he was like a tantrum-throwing kid...
Tirzad... Adventure... Could it be...

response.speaker: Kalantari
response.text: Sorry for interrupting your conversation. I'm Kalantari, a student in the Akademiya. I seek traces of the past that remain on the earth.

response.speaker: Kalantari
response.text: Were you part of Tirzad Hindi's recent expedition in the desert?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? How did you know?

response.speaker: Kalantari
response.text: It really is you! He mentioned both of you in the acknowledgments of his paper.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paper? Oh yeah, he did say he would focus on writing his paper once he got back. So it's done already?

response.speaker: Kalantari
response.text: Yup, he locked himself in his room once he got back from the desert. The other researchers were worried that he was depressed from failing to obtain any results from his expedition.

response.speaker: Kalantari
response.text: After a few days, we started betting on whether he would eat or drink first when he finally came outside. But he suddenly charged out and submitted a paper to the Akademiya...

response.speaker: Kalantari
response.text: "The Golden Slumber: A Study on Governance in the Later Period of Al-Ahmar's Civilization and Stages of Survival."

response.speaker: Kalantari
response.text: It may sound a little rude, but I never expected Tirzad to be capable of writing such a groundbreaking paper.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Groundbreaking"? That sounds very impressive...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Heehee! That means Paimon's also very impressive!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, how did he thank us in that groundbreaking paper of his?

response.speaker: Kalantari
response.text: Hmm, let me think... It was at the end of the paper, so I can still remember it very clearly.

response.speaker: Kalantari
response.text: #"I'd like to dedicate this last paragraph to a Traveler and {M#his}{F#her} companion. They are like the corollas that blossom in the nursery, the bread and salt during a long trip, as well as a gift to me from the desert.

response.speaker: Kalantari
response.text: Without them, I, in no way, could complete this paper."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Whoa! {NICKNAME}! Tirzad really flattered us there. "A gift from the desert," huh? Paimon's blushing!

response.speaker: Kalantari
response.text: No, you deserve the praise. Anyone who helps a researcher during the paper writing process is worthy of acknowledgement and gratitude.

response.speaker: Kalantari
response.text: In the world of researchers, there's nothing more painful than writing a paper. If there is, it'll be getting stuck writing a paper.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Tirzad was worrying about his paper when we first met. He'd probably suffered quite a bit before then...

response.speaker: Kalantari
response.text: To tell you the truth, lately, I've been trapped in that state of suffering as well. I decided to enter the desert, thinking that perhaps I could make some new discoveries based on Tirzad's thesis.

response.speaker: Kalantari
response.text: I didn't expect to meet the very person featured in his acknowledgments. It must be fate that brought us together. So... can you help me like how you helped him...?

response.speaker: Kalantari
response.text: Awesome! I knew taking a day off and coming to Aaru Village would be the right choice!

response.speaker: Kalantari
response.text: Allow me to give you two a warm welcome. How does treating you to a meal sound? Of course, you'll be well compensated for your trouble. Whatever Tirzad paid, I'll... Uh, let's discuss that later!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yay! Delicious food and Mora!

response.speaker: Kalantari
response.text: Oh, are you perhaps exhausted and in need of some rest after your last adventure? Or did Tirzad's lack of common sense leave you with a bitter taste?

response.speaker: Kalantari
response.text: It's alright, I understand your pains. After all, it isn't easy for adventurers who travel the world to deal with researchers.

response.speaker: Kalantari
response.text: But I'm different. I'm from a family of merchants in Port Ormos. I'm nothing like those researchers who don't even know how to communicate with people.

response.speaker: Kalantari
response.text: Well, allow me to give you two a warm welcome. How does treating you to a meal sound? Of course, you'll be well compensated for your trouble. Whatever he paid, I'll... Uh, let's discuss that later!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hmm, getting paid and treated to a meal sure sounds like a good deal. {NICKNAME}, let's help him out.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: If you insist...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe.

choices.text: That's an Indoorsology researcher for you...

response.speaker: Kalantari
response.text: Indoorsology researcher...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup, Tirzad did call himself an Indoorsology researcher when we first met.

response.speaker: Kalantari
response.text: Indoorsology? I didn't see any mention of that in the paper... I guess I'll have to ask him when I get back.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yes, we'll definitely meet Jeht again as long as we continue adventuring.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: As for Tirzad... We can find him in the Akademiya. He calls himself an Indoorsology researcher, after all...

dialogues.text: Ka-lan-ta-ri!

dialogues.speaker: Kalantari
dialogues.text: Huh? That voice sounds really familiar...
Kalantari, I didn't expect you to sneak all the way to Aaru Village. This old bag of bones is going to fall apart chasing after you, you know?

dialogues.speaker: Kalantari
dialogues.text: Oh, it's Mr. Soheil! Someone at your age should be reading through texts and records in the Akademiya. What are you doing all the way out here?

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: Hmph! What am I doing here? I'm here to stop you youngsters from running off into the desert, of course!

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: All of you have read quite a few papers, yet you can't keep your cool. Tirzad gains some success once, and you all go charging into the desert like mindless Fungi.

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: The sage is afraid you'll alert the matra and worried that you might damage the ruins, so I was sent to dissuade all of you.

dialogues.speaker: Kalantari
dialogues.text: All of us...? But I came alone, and I even specially applied for paid leave to keep it a secret from everyone else.

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: You did come here alone, but you're not the only one with the same idea. Do you know how many leave applications the sage received yesterday?

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: Forty-six! A total of forty-six applications! All of them from young students wanting to try their luck after reading that paper!

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: They gave all sorts of excuses. Helping a neighbor whose house caught on fire, a Fungi invasion turning their homes upside down, accidentally consuming spoiled curry... If only they used their creativity on writing papers!

choices.text: Could it just be a coincidence?

response.speaker: Kalantari
response.text: Exactly! I mean, so many people supposedly applied for leave, but I didn't see a single one of them here in Aaru Village.

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: Of course you didn't! I have already convinced all forty-five of them to go back while on my way here. You're the last one.

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: Listen. Academic research never relies on luck. Tirzad may have produced a well-written paper, but we still haven't verified its credibility.

response.speaker: Kalantari
response.text: But... I've found a guide...

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: No buts! Having no prior experience is enough to get you lost in the desert. Even if you don't get lost, there's no guarantee you won't accidentally damage something within the ruins.

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: For the sake of your safety and the ruins', you must head back. If you refuse, I'll have to ask Hulwani from the Corps of Thirty to "escort" you back.

response.speaker: Hulwani
response.text: Please head back.

response.speaker: Kalantari
response.text: Uh... Alright...

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: That's how a researcher of the Akademiya should act. Alright, off you go.

response.speaker: Kalantari
response.text: Huh? Mr. Soheil, you're not going back?

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: Of course not. I'll be staying here for some time to stop other rash researchers like you from entering the desert.

response.speaker: Kalantari
response.text: I'm not rash... I—I'm just in need of inspiration for my paper. *sigh* I thought I finally had my chance.

response.speaker: Kalantari
response.text: Goodbye, Traveler, and may we meet again. Safe travels.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Being unable to write a paper really does seem like torture...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We didn't even get our free food...

choices.text: What a vast assortment of excuses.

response.speaker: Kalantari
response.text: And that's exactly why you should trust them. As they say, the absurdity of the truth often exceeds any researcher's imagination.

response.speaker: Kalantari
response.text: Besides, I haven't seen any other researcher here in Aaru Village, so there's a high chance they were all telling the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: Sorry, I was so busy with Kalantari that I didn't get to greet you. I'm Soheil from the Usaibia family, and a researcher from Vahumana.

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: Did he plan to hire you as his guide? In that case, I'm sorry for ruining your business.

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: But it may not be a bad thing. Tirzad's paper isn't very credible, so you might have ended up going all the way for nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No, I believe him.

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: Oh? Why are you so sure? Wait. Are you... the ones mentioned in his acknowledgments...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Yes, that's us. We're the famed {NICKNAME} and Paimon, the travelers who went on an expedition with Tirzad!

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: Hmm, well. Being willing to support your employer is a good thing, I suppose. It shows that you value contracts just as the people of Liyue do. But you can't fool me.

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: I've been to the desert in my youth, but I have never once encountered places like the "Khemenu Temple" or "Khaj-Nisut" mentioned in that paper.

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: Besides that, the sandstorm at the top of the Mausoleum of King Deshret is still as I remember it from my youth. So, I suspect that Tirzad never entered the Mausoleum of King Deshret. He probably made it all up.

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: I'm fairly certain you took his Mora and got your stories straight so that when someone comes to check, his paper would seem more credible.

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: It might have been a good plan, but unfortunately, you ran into me.

choices.text: That's not the kind of person he is.

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: You don't understand researchers. I've seen so many researchers who appear to be honorable yet are shameless in private. What do you think the matra are for?

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: Anyway, you're free to go. I won't pursue the matter. Just... don't help him write fake theses anymore.

response.speaker: Hulwani
response.text: Please leave.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, Paimon's so peeved! Paimon could sense him looking down on us beneath that polite tone!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He even said that about Tirzad! That was too much! He's saying we faked it just because he couldn't find a way into the ruins himself!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ohh! Have you been taking good care of the stone slate Tirzad left with us?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's right here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Perfect! That's an important piece of evidence!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Wait a minute... The symbol at its center has lit up! And it's pointing somewhere...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're right... In that case, we might be able to enter the depths of the ruins now. Y'know, the place we couldn't enter before.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's go and take a look. If we find any solid evidence, that researcher will have no choice but apologize to Tirzad and us!

choices.text: It's probably because we finished King Deshret's trial.

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: Well, I certainly believe that you're not easily tempted by Mora, so Tirzad must have made an offer that you couldn't refuse.

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: I've seen many researchers who would stop at nothing just to complete their papers.

talks.objective: Go to the location indicated by the stone slate

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: According to the stone slate, we've arrived at our destination!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's just that... Paimon doesn't see any special devices, even though we're definitely inside the Mausoleum now. Have we gone the wrong way?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Should we have another look at the stone slate?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? There's new writing on it... And three dots of light...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "The mortal plane is like a river between the underworld and Aaru. Mortals must not cross, must not probe, must not... Uh... Must not... Paimon doesn't know how to read that... or they shall descend into the underworld forever..."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "In order to ascend to Aaru, one must have a body like that of a vulture and soar above the underworld... Peck at three different organs in order to obtain the consent of Al-Ahmar, and fly across the river in the form of a falcon..."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That word is "covet."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... "Must not covet." But what does that mean? This all sounds pretty important, but Paimon doesn't understand anything.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Which one do you think is more important, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: In order to ascend to Aaru... Does that mean Aaru Village? But Paimon doesn't think Aaru Village existed back then... Anyway, shouldn't the opposite of the underworld be a really wonderful place?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, if we sum it all up, we must do something to the "organs" to open a new path that leads to "Aaru." Um... It all sounds kinda mysterious...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But speaking of "organs"... Paimon thinks we've heard that one somewhere.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! That guy was so stubborn then! He wouldn't listen to anyone and kept saying that King Deshret's legacy had to be in King Deshret's Mausoleum...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then he went into a hall that he said was meant to store some "organs" and found a strange device. After that, the symbols on the stone slate just "clicked" and lit up.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Maybe "Peck at three different organs" refers to finding three devices just like before, and then we'll get to that place called "Aaru"!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's go! Let's see what secrets King Deshret has been hiding in "Aaru"!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! Paimon remembers now! Tirzad made us go to some hall used to store "organs," didn't he?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He was so stubborn then! He wouldn't listen to anyone and insisted that King Deshret's legacy had to be in King Deshret's Mausoleum. Then he found a strange device.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But in the end, it was wise ol' Paimon who discovered the link between the stone slate and the strange device, and made the symbol on the stone slate go "click" and light up!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sounds like you might have embellished things a little...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, only a little! Anyway, the "organs" are the important part. Let's not dwell on the details!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Peck out three organ types... Do we really have to eat... organs...? That's scary...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Obtaining the consent of Al-Ahmar should refer to opening a new path.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon has been thinking for a while now... This place feels really important... It's like Stormterror's Lair but in the desert!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon wonders if bards sang about this place during King Deshret's reign... Let's get a closer look.

talks.objective: Follow the stone slate's guidance and obtain full clearance

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, is this... "Aaru"?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, according to the stone slate, we've obtained King Deshret's consent and reached "Aaru."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But this place doesn't seem very much like "Aaru." There's only this frighteningly huge device. Paimon feels that "Aaru" should be more... more...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, that's right! It should be a place with a ton of delicious food!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, at a time like this, another look at the stone slate couldn't hurt. ...Huh? There's a new line of words here!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "After flying across the river in falcon form, one must burn the embers of the sun at three places using feathers. Only through this may one obtain the mercy of Al-Ahmar and ascend to Aaru."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* There's more... Paimon's getting annoyed. Why can't King Deshret just finish explaining without stopping? This is getting exhausting.

choices.text: Don't forget about how Tirzad was maligned.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right. That's right! We're here to make that Soheil guy apologize!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, it isn't time to head back yet. Let's find out how to "burn the embers of the sun."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! You're right! The longer the adventure, the better the treasure. It's a pattern Paimon's discovered after many adventures, hehe! We should be glad this is taking so long!

choices.text: I'm so tired, let's head back...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay... But wait, we're here to make that annoying researcher, Soheil, apologize. He'll laugh at us if we head back now!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, exactly! It should at least be filled with greenery like Sumeru City!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right, it doesn't look much different from the underworld we just passed through, and Paimon even sees a frighteningly huge device up ahead. Paimon feels that "Aaru" should be more... more...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, that's right! It should be a place with a ton of delicious food!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, exactly! It should at least be filled with greenery like Sumeru City!

talks.objective: Follow the stone slate's guidance and obtain full clearance
Follow the stone slate's guidance and obtain full clearance
Head to the Great Hall of Truths following the guidance of the slate

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: Huh? Why are you still in Aaru Village? Are you thinking about trying to get something from me?

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: Just give up on that. I'm not Tirzad, Kalantari, or any of those other youngsters. I never try to take the easy way out.

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: Allow me to guide you to the right path. Start gaining knowledge now. Who knows, you might even make it into the Akademiya once you reach my age.

talks.objective: Explore the area and find a way to activate the giant device

dialogues.speaker: Hulwani
dialogues.text: Please leave. Don't do anything unnecessary.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still, Paimon thinks that those three dots of light on the stone slate include places we have been to. Their symbols have lit up too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Great, just thinking about going to three separate places made Paimon tired, but it looks like we just have to find one more device. Paimon is so grateful to past Paimon.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Be grateful to me too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Right, thank you, {NICKNAME}! Let's go look for the remaining devices!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! Paimon remembers now! Tirzad made us go to some hall used to store "organs," didn't he?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He was so stubborn then! He wouldn't listen to anyone and insisted that King Deshret's legacy had to be in King Deshret's Mausoleum. Then he found a strange device.

dialogues.speaker: Hulwani
dialogues.text: No, I refuse to escort you into the desert.

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: But the Mausoleum of King Deshret, which has remained the same for centuries, has undergone an unprecedented change. You saw it too just now, didn't you? I need to make a record...

dialogues.speaker: Hulwani
dialogues.text: It's also my first time seeing this change... However, the sage has prohibited researchers from entering the desert without his permission.

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: I—I'm not like those rash young researchers. I've dedicated years to studying in the Akademiya...

dialogues.speaker: Hulwani
dialogues.text: The answer is still "no."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello, long time no see. Seems like you're having a nice time in Aaru Village!

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: Huh? What are the two of you doing here? I did say that I wouldn't pursue the matter, but you should stop going around deceiving people.

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: I'm getting old, so my time is way more precious than yours. Besides, I have more important business to attend to. So, if you would excuse me.

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: No! Not at all! I would never go against the sage's restrictions! I just want to...

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: Wait a minute, both of you are all covered in dirt, and you're holding a suspicious stone slate... Did you just return from the desert, by any chance?

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: Are the... changes in the Mausoleum of King Deshret... linked to you?

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: How can that be? Generations of Vahumana researchers tried everything they could to open the mausoleum's entrance and discover the secrets within, yet none succeeded. But you two easily...

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: Can I take a look at the stone slate you brought back with you?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sure.

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: Thank you. The forest will remember your generosity!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Soheil's eyes open wide as he scans the stone slate from every angle. Even his breathing and speech speed up slightly.

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: Due to various reasons, practically all the records of the later period of Al-Ahmar's civilization have been lost. Even those that are occasionally dug up are just fragments. I've never seen such a perfect stone slate!

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: No, it's not only me. Even the sage may have never witnessed such a... miracle.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph! You were calling us frauds just a short while ago!

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: Did you really enter the Mausoleum of King Deshret as Tirzad's paper described?

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: I—It really is true then...

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: In the name of Vahumana researcher Soheil and on behalf of my family, I sincerely apologize. I hope you'll be so kind as to forgive my greatest mistake — ignorance.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Whoa, what a sudden change of attitude! It's like he's taken on a completely different character, just like the storytellers of Liyue do.)

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: Could you... allow me to carefully inspect that stone slate? I'll compensate both of you for it!

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: As for the amount... Hmm... Before that, let's go someplace quiet so I can take a closer look at that slate.

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: Please stop joking. I've always thought highly of Tirzad and considered him the future of Vahumana. I'm not in the least surprised that he wrote such a wonderful paper.

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: Besides, he received a "gift from the desert" — the assistance of an outstanding traveler like you!

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: Hah! I knew it! Wait... Wh—where did you get this stone slate from?

choices.text: Wanna get closer to the Mausoleum of King Deshret?

talks.objective: Defeat the "big guy with evil intentions"
Return to Aaru Village and talk to Soheil

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still, Paimon thinks that those three dots of light on the stone slate include places we have been to. Their symbols have lit up too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Awesome! Just thinking about going to three separate places made Paimon tired, but it looks like we only have to find two more devices. Paimon is so grateful to Past-Paimon, hehe!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Be grateful to me too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Right, thank you, {NICKNAME}! Let's go look for the remaining devices!
